newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane builds on intraday gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane builds on intraday gains.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices built upon intraday gains in late trade on Thursday, following NYMEX heating oil higher amid continued anticipation of good crop drying demand, traders said.
The U.S. Midwest largely led the market as cool weather in the hub triggered concerns of an early crop harvest -- meaning wetter than usual crops -- and reminded players that winter lays ahead.
In Conway, Kansas, hub, spot propane traded at 53.25 cents a gallon, a quarter cent higher than at midday, bringing the total day's gain to 1.50 cents.
Mont Belvieu, Texas, was talked between 51.50/51.75 cents, also a quarter cent above earlier activity and 1.50 cent above Wednesday values.
"With Conway going up, some people see Belvieu poised to make a run," said one U.S. trader, adding that strong heating oil futures and low inventories are helping to support the Gulf market.
Some traders say they expect crop drying demand to kick in hard sometime next week due to the cold weather.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
